On 27 April 2024, Last Generation activists staged a protest at the airport in Stuttgart (Baden-Wurttemberg), some covering themselves in fake blood and laying down in front of the entrance area as if dead, to draw attention to what they consider unjust subsidies for climate-damaging air travel and to demand the removal of short-haul destinations from the program and a ban on private jets from 2026. The activists also accused the airport, the city and the state of greenwashing and dishonesty in fulfilling their legal climate protection mandate. Another group of Last Generation activists staged a protest at Marienplatz and distributed food previously taken from supermarkets' garbage containers to draw attention to the issue of food waste in the face of rising prices and increasing food shortages worldwide and to the lack of a legal framework to curb food waste.

The participants, including members of the LGBTQ+ community, demanded increased support for those who experience harassment and assault in nightlife settings.

The participants accused politicians and the media of lies and false reporting intended to brand all Muslims in Germany as Islamists against the backdrop of the Gaza war.

On 29 April 2024, students staged a protest in front of the vocational college for business and administration in Leverkusen (Nordrhein-Westfalen) against racism and right-wing extremism.

On 6 August 2024, at the call of 'ZORA Berlin and Palestine at the forefront', up to 120 to around 150 people gathered outside the courthouse in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), to protest in support of a 22-year-old woman who was convicted of incitement to hatred for using the pro-Palestinian slogan 'From the River to the Sea' at a demonstration in October 2023. Protesters criticized the trial and increased security measures as repressive.

On 4 August 2024, around 30 people, including speakers from 'International Physicians for the Prevention of Nuclear War' (IPPNW), 'Network at the Tower' (Netzwerk am Turm), and 'Active for Peace' (Aktiv fur Frieden), gathered in Bad Kreuznach (Rheinland-Pfalz), to commemorate the 79th anniversary of the Hiroshima bombing and to warn about the high risk of a potential nuclear war, while protesting against discussions about stationing nuclear-armed missiles in Germany and the financing of the Ukraine war.

On 9 August 2024, employees of ThyssenKrupp Steel held a demonstration in front of the ThyssenKrupp Steel headquarters in Duisburg (Nordrhein-Westfalen) against the planned job cuts and capacity reduction program expected to be announced at an upcoming board meeting. Protesters carried out the symbolic action of carrying a coffin representing the CEO, carried torches, and placed wooden crosses in front of the headquarters.

source: Hessische Niedersachsische Allgemeine; Solinger Tageblatt; Suddeutsche Zeitung
notes: On 4 August 2024, around 15 environmental activists from the group 'Climate Justice Kassel' (Klimagerechtigkeit Kassel), staged a protest at the water displays in Bergpark Wilhelmshohe in Kassel (Hessen). They dyed the water on the cascades bright green to draw attention to the controversial salt discharge into the Werra river by the Kassel-based salt and fertilizer producer K+S, and unfurled a banner reading 'Drinking water instead of toxic water', to raise awareness about water pollution.

On 8 August 2024, around 40 people participated in a protest, organized by a newly formed initiative called 'Together Against War' (Gemeinsam gegen den Krieg), in Dippoldiswalde (Sachsen) against military escalation and the potential reintroduction of conscription. Furthermore, the participants protested the increased calls by politicians for rearmament and demanded a ban on the German Armed Forces' presence in Saxony schools and job fairs, and the introduction of civil clause in Saxony's universities and colleges to prevent military involvement. The Left party was involved.

On 7 August 2024, around 1,500 people participated in a demonstration via forming a human chain in the Glockenbach Quarter of Munchen (Bayern) as a show of solidarity following a transphobic graffiti attack on the queer cultural centers SUB (Gay Communication and Cultural Center) and LeZ (Lesbian-Queer Center). The demonstration was organized in response to the messages such as 'Kill all Trans,' that were found on the buildings. The event was called and organized by CSD Munich and various queer organizations, such as LesCommunity, diversity Munchen, Rosa Lista, Munchner Aids-Help, to protest against anti-queer violence and support the LGBTIQ+ community.

On 14 August 2024, members of DFG-VK gathered at the Stadionbad in Koln (Nordrhein-Westfalen), to protest against a large advertisement for the Bundeswehr (German Army), criticizing it for promoting military service at a family-oriented location. They protested by occupying the ten-meter diving platform.

On 15 August 2024, around 30 activists from the AfgActivistCollective staged a protest camp at Alexanderplatz in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), to raise awareness about the oppression in Afghanistan, marking the third anniversary of the Taliban's takeover of Afghanistan. The camp featured a 'Ban Taliban' banner.

On 16 August 2024, a group of elderly people gathered in Elsfleth (Niedersachsen), to protest against the removal of a popular blue bench by the city administration, which was intended to prevent vandalism.

On 15 August 2024, at the call of Luisa Neubauer from Fridays For Future, more than 100 Fridays for Future activists and other organizations staged a protest outside the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), to protest against the recent approval of gas drilling in the North Sea near Borkum, citing the threat it poses to the environment and the Wattenmeer, a UNESCO World Heritage site. The protesters urged the German government to reconsider the decision and address the international agreements with the Netherlands. This protest was part of the 'Oil Kills' campaign, which aims for the elimination of oil, gas, and coal by 2030 and for the need for increased climate protection.

On 10 August 2024, between 300 and 1,000 people joined a protest organized by Fridays for Future on Borkum (Niedersachsen) against a planned gas extraction project, aiming to prevent the Dutch company One-Dyas from starting drilling operations in the North Sea, which the group described as a threat to a nature reserve as well as the beginning of a new era of fossil fuel exploitation, contracting Germany's climate commitments.

On 8 August 2024, around 600 people gathered for a protest, organized by the citizen's initiative 'Good Health Care in Raiffeisenland' (Gute Gesundheitsversorgung im Raiffeisenland), outside of the hospital in Altenkirchen (Rheinland-Pfalz), voicing their discontent with what they describe as betrayal regarding promised healthcare services and the cuts to medical services at the hospital and expressing concerns over the decline in healthcare quality in the region.

On 9 August 2024, residents of Erfurt-Niedernissa gathered at a local bus stop on Rudolfstadter Street in Erfurt (Thuringen) for a protest with open umbrellas to express their frustration over the long-delayed repair of the bus stop's roof, which was damaged by a truck accident in December 2023, demanding the immediate repair of the shelter, emphasizing that passengers, including school children, have been left exposed to rain for nearly eight months.

On 14 August 2024, 6 Last Generation activists staged a protest at the Airport in Munchen (Bayern) against the use of oil and kerosene, holding a large banner with the message 'Oil, gas, and kerosene are driving the world to ruin' in the terminal. The protest was peaceful.

On 10 August 2024, around 650 people gathered to participate in the 'Hanfparade' ('Cannabis parade') with the motto 'Legalisation, but the right way!' at Alexander Square in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), advocating for more comprehensive legalization of cannabis and demanding broader access to cannabis, including the implementation of licensed cannabis retail stores beyond the current model that restricts sales to Cannabis Social Clubs.

On 10 August 2024, around 80 people gathered at Marienplatz in Munchen (Bayern) for a protest titled 'Randgruppenkrawall' (Marginalized Groups Riot'), organized by the Association for people with disabilities Bayern (Behindertenverband Bayern), calling for better implementation of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, emphasizing the need for greater inclusion and criticizing the ongoing marginalization, paternalism, and oppression of people with disabilities in Germany.

On 10 August 2024, 14 activists from the climate group Last Generation (Letzte Generation) staged a protest at the airport in Stuttgart (Baden-Wurttemberg), aiming to raise awareness about the environmental impact of air travel and to oppose the criminalization of climate activists, criticizing the government for encouraging airport expansion and subsidizing airlines.

On 10 August 2024, around 30 activists from Last Generation (Germany) staged a protest at Kassel Airport in Calden (Hessen), opposing government subsidies for flights, criticizing the use of EUR 130,000 in taxpayer money to subsidize 500 flight tickets, furthermore expressing solidarity with activists who faced house searches after a similar protest at Franfurt am Main airport. They protested for climate protection with slogans such as 'Oil kills'.

On 10 August 2024, members of Last Generation staged a protest at Dortmund (Nordrhein-Westfalen) airport, holding up signs reading 'Oil kills,' pouring black-tinted adhesive on the terminal floor to symbolize oil, raising awareness about the environmental damage caused by domestic flights, highlighting the harmful impact of fossil fuels. Police initiated legal proceedings against 20 individuals for trespassing and violations of assembly law but didn't intervene.

On 10 August 2024, over 1,000 people participated in the Christopher Street Day (CSD) parade in Bautzen (Sachsen) despite of the intensified atmosphere due to counter-protests. At the call of Free Saxony, around 680 far-right protesters gathered to protest against the CSD celebrations, which led to heightened tensions but no physical interaction and a large police presence. The far-right protesters organized under the slogan 'Against Gender Propaganda and Identity Confusion,' aimed at disrupting the CSD.

On 10 August 2024, two groups simultaneously staged counter-protests in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin), one to demanding the release of Israeli hostages and to call for protection of Jewish life in Berlin and one to demand the liberation of Palestine, criticizing the state of Israel and its policies. Police were deployed to separate the groups. Despite the tension between the two groups, no violent escalation and clashes, apart from counter-chanting, occurred.

On 10 August 2024, more than 13,000 people marched through Frankfurt am Main (Hessen) during the Christopher Street Day (CSD) celebration under the motto 'Wir sind extrem liebevoll' ('We are extremely loving'), celebrating queerness, demanding an end to queerphobia and discrimination as well as equal rights for all, while also promoting the visibility and acceptance of the LGBTIQ+ community.

On 11 August 2024, around 300 people gathered for a dancing protest, organized by Association Weimar Republic (Verein Weimarer Republik), on the Theatre Square in Weimar (Thuringen), advocating for democracy and openness to the world, as part of the commemoration of the former Constitution Day.

On 10 August 2024, around 200 people gathered in Hamburg - Harburg (Hamburg), marching from Edeka-Center on Seevegasse and proceeding to the refugee reception center on Harburger Poststrase, for a protest against the 'SocialCard,' a payment card for refugees, criticizing the card as discriminatory and repressive, arguing that it undermines refugee autonomy and fails to meet individual needs, highlighting recent legal challenges, such as a court ruling favoring a refugee who needed more than the allocated EUR 50 per month for living expenses.

On 11 August 2024, between around 1,500 and 4,000 people gathered in Muhlhausen/Thuringen (Thuringen) for a protest organized by a group called 'SEM group Unstrut-Hainich' (Mittelstandgruppe Unstrut-Hainisch), featuring controversial former ZDF news anchor Peter Hahne as a guest speaker, intending to send a political message to local and federal lawmakers, expressing frustration with bureaucratic delays as well as local and national policies affecting small businesses and communities, aiming to pressure politicians to serve their constituents better and address inefficiencies and regulatory burdens.

On 10 August 2024, around 5,000 people participated in a parade for Christopher Street Day (CSD) in Braunschweig (Niedersachsen), demanding justice, equal rights for LGBTIQ+ individuals, and the inclusion of diversity in Germany's Basic Law under the motto 'Dresscode Diversity - Justice into the Basic Law.' A group of 15 people gathered for a counter-demonstration using queerphobic statements. Counter-protesters were accompanied by the police to the main train station.

assoc_actor_1: Catholic Christian Group (Germany); Labor Group (Germany); OEDP: Ecological Democratic Party; VCD: Traffic Club Germany
notes: On 14 August 2024, at the call of the 'Catholic Workers' Movement' (Katholische Arbeitnehmer-Bewegung (KAB)), people, including members of VCD, and Chairman of the Catholic Deanery Council of Kempten Franz Josef Natterer-Babych (OEDP), gathered at the Allgau Festival Week in Kempten (Allgau) (Bayern), to protest for the rights of people with disabilities, focusing on their right to work, inclusive education, and better accessibility in Kempten, particularly at the main train station.

On 17 August 2024, at the international call of Maria Corina Machado, a prominent opposition leader in Venezuela, and at the call of the Venezuelan community, around 350 people staged a protest in Munchen (Bayern) against the Venezuelan government, aiming to raise awareness about human rights abuses and the authoritarian regime of Nicolas Maduro, urging international and German government action.

On 22 August 2024, around 100 representatives from home care services gathered in front of the State Parliament ('Landtag') in Magdeburg (Sachsen-Anhalt) to protest against the AOK Sachsen-Anhalt, General Local Health Insurance, during the first Landtag session after the summer break, continuing a series of protests regarding the AOK's refusal to adhere to an arbitration ruling that mandated increased payments to care services. The protest aimed to draw attention to the financial strain on care services and demand prompt action from both the AOK and the State Social Minister, Petra Grimm-Benne.

On 21 August 2024, around 20 citizens held a vigil, organized by the group 'Tree Guards' ('Baumwachter'), outside the Town Hall in Beuel in Bonn (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to protest the potential felling of an old Durch Linden tree located in Niederholtorf and to argue for the tree's preservation due to its environmental significance and contribution to the community's quality of life.

On 19 August 2024, people gathered outside the fuel element factory in Lingen (Niedersachsen), to protest against upcoming uranium deliveries from Russia. The Greens politicians, involved in the protest, warned of 'serious security issues and an incalculable risk' associated with these deliveries.

On 22 August 2024, around 140 people gathered for a protest and prayer outside of the Blue Mosque in Hamburg (Hamburg), in a series of Thursday and Friday protests and prayers, demanding the reopening of the mosque, sparked by the closure of the Mosque following the government's ban on the Islamic Centre Hamburg (IZH). The protesters sought to restore their right to religious practice and requested a special permit for ongoing gatherings.

On 23 August 2024, over 100 people gathered for a protest and prayer outside of the Blue Mosque in Hamburg (Hamburg), as a part of an ongoing effort to demand the reopening of the mosque, which was shut down following the ban on the Islamic Centre Hamburg (IZH) by the German government. The protesters demanded their right to freedom of religion and continued to seek a resolution that would allow them to practice their faith at the historic site.

On 22 August 2024, at least several dozen teachers, supported by GEW, staged a protest by blocking the intersection of Wall and Herdentor in Bremen (Bremen) during the afternoon rush hour, aimed to raise awareness about the impact of the ongoing budget freeze in the education sector, demanding the establishment of a 'special education fund' to address the rising number of students and the urgent need for additional resources in early childhood education, schools, and adult education.

assoc_actor_1: Labor Group (Germany); NGG: Food, Beverages and Catering Union
notes: On 20 August 2024, at the call of NGG, around 20 employees from the hotel and gastronomy industry gathered at the pier in Zinnowitz (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern), demanding higher wages due to increasing prices and rents. The protest was organized amidst ongoing tariff negotiations with the DEHOGA employer association and protesters highlighted the low wages in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern compared to neighboring Brandenburg, amid rising living costs in tourist hotspots.

On 22 August 2024, around 120 people gathered in Jena (Thuringen), marching from Holzmarkt through the city center, to protest against the occupation of Palestine and to voice their opposition to Israel's occupation of Palestinian territories, seeking to raise awareness and call for action in support of Palestinian rights. The protest was countered by a counter-protest with around 30 protesters, expressing solidarity with Israel.

assoc_actor_1: PETA: People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals
notes: On 22 August 2024, PETA activists staged a protest on Munsterlplatz in Ulm (Baden-Wurttemberg) to advocate for veganism as a crucial step toward climate protection. An activist, representing a 'human steak,' lay nearly naked on a large plate, covered in beetroot juice to simulate blood. This visual aimed to raise awareness about the environmental impact of meat consumption and to encourage people to adopt a vegan diet, highlighting the effects of the meat industry on the environment, stating that switching to plant-based diets could reduce emissions by up to 75%.

On 22 August 2024, several hundred Thyssenkrupp steelworkers staged a spontaneous protest and strike at the plant in Dortmund (Nordrhein-Westfalen), protesting against the company's plans to significantly reduce steel production, potentially leading to the loss of 10,000 jobs across various sites, to express their opposition to CEO Miguel Lopez's proposal to cut production and limit financial support for the steel division's transformation, and to highlight concerns over the future of their jobs and the stability of the company.

On 22 August 2024, between 350 and 400 Thyssenkrupp steelworkers gathered in a spontaneous assembly outside the Bruckhausen plant in Duisburg (Nordrhein-Westfalen), blocking the factory gates and adjacent streets, disrupting traffic for several hours, sparked by fears over potential job cuts, following reports that the company might reduce production capacities more drastically than previously announced, threatening up to 10,000 jobs. The workers, supported by the works council (Betriebsrat), expressed their determination not to be pressured by the company's management, which they describe to be out of touch with the realities of the steel industry.
On 17 August 2024, around 2,500 people participated in the Christopher Street Day (CSD) in Gottingen (Niedersachsen), to protest for LGBTQ+ rights and community visibility.

assoc_actor_1: Labor Group (Germany); NGG: Food, Beverages and Catering Union
notes: On 20 August 2024, at the call of NGG, around 450 to 500 employees from the confectionery industry gathered in Hamburg (Hamburg), demanding a 9.9% wage increase, or at least 360 euros per month, after the union canceled regional collective agreements.

On 16 August 2024, approximately 800 employees of the Hannover Medical School (MHH) gathered at the Arminia Stadium in Hannover (Niedersachsen), to protest the stagnation in negotiations for a new collective agreement. The health workers are demanding a new tariff agreement focused on 'relief' in response to ongoing issues in the healthcare sector.

assoc_actor_1: BUND: German Federation for the Environment and Nature Conservation; Evangelical Christian Group (Germany)
notes: On 17 August 2024, at the call of the youth environmental network JANUN, BUNDjugend Niedersachsen, and the Evangelical Youth of Oldenburg, under the motto 'Amo(o)re for Moore', people participated in a Silent Climate Parade through Oldenburg (Niedersachsen), to protest against the planned Fliegerhorststrase, which they argue would destroy valuable wetlands and release significant amounts of CO2. The protesters demanded sustainable transportation alternatives.

source: Die Tageszeitung; Hannoversche Allgemeine; Mitteldeutschen Zeitung; Passauer Neue Presse; Suddeutsche Zeitung
notes: On 17 August 2024, around 21,000 gathered in Leipzig (Sachsen) on the occasion of Christopher Street Day (CSD) and to promote the LGBT community's rights. Before the demonstration, around 300 to 400 far-right and neo-Nazi protesters had gathered at the train station under the motto 'proud, German, national' with the purpose of staging a counter-protest. However, they were cordoned off by the police, who also carried out identity checks, and their march did not take place.

On 22 August 2024, around 170 people gathered near the Garnison Church in Potsdam (Brandenburg) to stage a protest against the controversial reopening of the church tower, marking their protest with chants such as 'Hypocrites, hypocrites', aimed at the event's attendees, including prominent figures such as German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, who praised the project as a symbol of critical historical awareness. The protest was motivated by the church's historical association with Nazi Germany and concerns were the use of public funds for its reconstruction.

On 11 August 2024, around 100 cyclists participated in a protest in Ramstein-Miesenbach (Rheinland-Pfalz), advocating for peace and global nuclear disarmament as well as raising awareness about the dangers of nuclear weapons, as part of the Nuclear ban initiative, which underscores the urgency of peace efforts in light of the Doomsday Clock's alarming proximity to midnight.

On 24 August 2024, around 23,000 people participated in the Christopher Street Day (CSD) parade in Bremen (Bremen) to advocate for the rights of the LGBTQ+ community. The event, centered around the theme 'What do we still want? To be ourselves, to live freely!', emphasized the demand for equality and acceptance for lesbian, gay, and queer individuals. While the protest was predominantly peaceful, there were minor incidents, including a few cases of queerphobic insults and threats, which were addressed by the police.

On 24 August 2024, several hundred people, including Ukrainian community members, participated in a protest in Dortmund (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to mark Ukraine's Independence Day. The protesters, carrying a yellow-and-blue banner representing the Ukrainian flag, marched through the city center, causing temporary traffic disruptions on the Wallring. The protest aimed to show solidarity with Ukraine amidst the ongoing conflict with Russia, emphasizing support for Ukrainian sovereignty and freedom.

On 24 August 2024, around 2,600 people participated in a protest and parade in the framework of the Christopher Street Day (CSD) in Magdeburg (Sachsen-Anhalt) to demand equality, respect, and to oppose discrimination against the LGBTQ+ community. Alongside the main event, a far-right counter-protest of about 250 people took place, during which some participants used symbols associated with unconstitutional organizations, such as neo-Nazi symbolics banned under German law. Furthermore, there were instances of verbal abuse directed at participants of the CSD. This included derogatory remarks or offensive language aimed at LGBTQ+ protesters. This prompted police investigations.

On 28 August 2024, pharmacists gathered in Erfurt (Thuringen), to protest against the reform plans proposed by Federal Health Minister Karl Lauterbach (SPD). The protesters aimed to address issues such as improving economic conditions, ensuring pharmacist presence in pharmacies, and reducing bureaucratic obstacles.

On 24 August 2024, around 4,000 people participated in a protest in Koln (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to mark Ukraine's Independence Day, organized by the German-Ukrainian association Blue-Yellow-Cross (Blau-Gelbes Kreuz). The protest, held under the motto 'Resolutely support Ukraine and defend a free Europe,' aimed to show solidarity with Ukraine amidst the ongoing war. Political figures such as Berivan Aymaz and Mona Neubaur were present, with speeches and musical performances highlighting the event. Similar protests took place in Dusseldorf and Bonn, gathering smaller crowds.

On 24 August 2024, around 600 people participated in a protest during the Christopher Street Day (CSD) parade in Krefeld (Nordrhein-Westfalen). The event aimed to advocate for the rights of LGBTQ+ individuals and promote a message of tolerance and diversity. The parade participants moved through the city, culminating at the Von-der-Leyen-Platz, where a moment of silence was held to honor the victims of a recent knife attack in Solingen.
On 28 August 2024, at the call of Free Saxony, around 400 people gathered in Bad Gottleuba-Berggiesshubel (Sachsen), to protest against the presence of refugees in the area.

On 24 August 2024, around 400 people participated in a protest march, under the title 'Solidarity with Palestine - Stop the Genocide - No Weapons for Israel,' from Neptunenbrunnen near Alexanderplatz until Leipziger Platz in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), expressing solidarity with Palestine and calling a cessation of arms sales to Israel. Two men were arrested, because, according to the police, they engaged in criminal acts during previous protests. The protest march was stopped at some point due to 30 youths chanting slogans described as incitement to hatred. One person was arrested. One more person was arrested later on. The police report that this was the case due to chanting slogans that are evaluated as incitement to hatred by the police.
On 24 August 2024, over 500 people gathered for a protest at the Brandenburger Tor in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) to celebrate Ukraine's Independence Day and to show solidarity with Ukraine.

On 24 August 2024, around 500 people participated in a protest march to the German Federal Chancellery in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), advocating for the protection of religious freedom under the slogan 'Defend Religious Freedom: Hands Off Our Places of Worship!' The protest took place with a significant police presence of approximately 700 officers actively monitoring the city center.

On 24 August 2024, around 1,700 to 3,000 participants took part in the Christopher Street Day (CSD) parade in Jena (Thuringen), celebrating queer rights under the motto 'Thuringen stays colorful!' ('Thuringen bleibt bunt!').

On 24 August 2024, approximately 430 people participated in the Christopher Street Day (CSD) event in Plauen (Sachsen), celebrating queer rights and advocating for tolerance and diversity. There are reports of one participant being insulted and another being threatened. Simultaneously, a counter-protest titled 'Against Gender Propaganda and Identity Confusion,' with around 75 participants, was restricted to a stationary gathering at Rathenauplatz due to concerns about the reliability of the organizers. This counter-protest ended prematurely, and post-event, some participants engaged in xenophobic rhetoric, leading to identity checks and charges of incitement to hatred against 18 individuals.

On 29 August 2024, several hundred Thyssenkrupp Steel employees protested at the company's headquarters in Duisburg (Nordrhein-Westfalen), to protest against the planned restructuring and potential job cuts amid escalating conflicts within the company's leadership, coinciding with a supervisory board meeting where significant personnel decisions were anticipated.

On 24 August 2024, around 350 Ukrainians and supporters gathered for a protest on Burgplatz in Leipzig (Sachsen) to mark the 33rd anniversary of Ukraine's independence, to express solidarity with Ukraine, oppose the ongoing Russian invasion, and highlight the war's proximity to Europe. Participants, including many women, children, and youth, held signs condemning Russian war crimes and emphasizing that the conflict affects Europe as well.

On 24 August 2024, around 30 activists from the climate protection group Last Generation (Germany) staged a protest in Park Sanssouci in Potsdam (Brandenburg), highlighting the impacts of climate change. The protest involved holding banners with messages like 'Renot with coal, oil, and gas' and lying down on the ground. The action was part of their effort to draw attention to the severe effects of climate change on the park, which has seen significant damage due to extensive heat and drought. The protest was organized to pressure the government to take stronger action against climate change.

On 30 August 2024, Free Saxony supporters gathered at a campaign event in Chemnitz (Sachsen) where German Chancellor Olaf Scholz spoke, disrupting Scholz's speech and opposing his stance on migration and other policies.

On 30 August 2024, Last Generation activists gathered at the Allgau Airport in Memmingen (Bayern), using banners and symbolic actions to oppose the heavy subsidization of air travel. The protest did not disrupt flights but aimed to highlight issues like greenwashing in the aviation industry.

On 24 August 2024, around 250 Ukrainians and supporters gathered in the city center of Heidelberg (Baden-Wurttemberg) to mark Ukraine's 33rd Independence Day with a protest organized by the Coalition Ukrainian Organizations in the Are of Rhein-Neackar (Bundnis ukrainischer Organisationen im Rhein-Neckar-Raum), with participants marching from the park near the Stadtbucherei to Universitatsplatz to highlight the ongoing Russian aggression against Ukraine and aimed to show solidarity with Ukraine, demanding comprehensive military aid, an end to Russian oil and gas imports, and the release of Ukrainian prisoners of war and civilians.

On 30 August 2024, around 80 people from the Muslim community gathered near the closed Blue Mosque in Hamburg - Hamburg-Nord (Hamburg), opposing its shutdown by the German government. The protesters held a public prayer and voiced their discontent over the mosque's closure following the ban of its operator, the Islamic Centre Hamburg, for alleged extremism and ties to Iran.

assoc_actor_1: Labor Group (Germany); Ver.di: United Services Union
notes: On 30 August 2024, at the call of Ver.di, around 300 employees of the Hamburger Hafen und Logistik AG (HHLA) protested at the Hamburg Port in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg), demanding a social tariff agreement in response to concerns over potential job cuts due to planned automation and restructuring at the port's Burchardkai container terminal.
On 28 August 2024, people gathered in Schleiz (Thuringen), to protest against the closure of the Sternbach hospital.

On 26 August 2024, tens of thousands of Borussia Dortmund (BVB) fans staged a protest during a home game at the Westfalenstadion in Dortmund (Nordrhein-Westfalen) against the club's sponsorship deal with Rheinmetall, a major arms manufacturer. The fans unfurled numerous protest banners in the stadium's South Stand, expressing their outrage over the partnership, which they believe contradicts the club's values of inclusivity and opposition to violence and discrimination. The protest was fueled by the belief that the deal prioritizes financial gain over the club's ethical principles.

On 27 August 2024, a group of citizens from the initiative Green North Dusseldorf (Gruner Norden Dusseldorf) protested in front of the District Committee meeting in Dusseldorf (Nordrhein-Westfalen) against the planned construction of a new residential area near Schloss Kalkum. The project, called 'Nordlich Kalkumer Schlossallee,' involves building 550 housing units, a school, sports facilities, and other infrastructure on 27 hectares of current farmland. The protesters oppose the project due to the environmental impact, particularly the loss of valuable land, and seek to preserve the area to counteract climate degradation.

On 27 August 2024, a group of former H&M call center employees gathered in front of the Amtsgericht in Nurnberg (Bayern) for a silent protest against the company's decision to terminate around 300 jobs and to close the call center in September. The protest, organized under the slogan 'We don't deserve this!', highlighted the workers' dissatisfaction and resistance to the impending layoffs, as they demanded fair treatment and job security.

On 27 August 2024, 55 people, including Ukrainian community members, participated in a protest titled 'Vigil for Ukraine' near Neumarkt in Chemnitz (Sachsen). This protest was organized to show solidarity with Ukraine and to emphasize the importance of supporting Ukraine amidst ongoing conflicts. During the event, a banner suspected of displaying unconstitutional symbols led to a police report, and a minor altercation occurred between a 51-year-old woman and a 62-year-old man, resulting in another police report.

On 6 September 2024, around 300 people participated in a protest in Kiel (Schleswig-Holstein) against the arms industry. Organized by the group 'Disarm Rheinmetall,' the protesters marched from their camp in Werftpark to the German Armed Forces barracks on Feldstrase and back. The event was part of a protest week aimed at highlighting the role of German arms production in global wars. A few protesters attempted to breach police barriers and used pyrotechnics, but the police pushed them back. The protest then proceeded. The protest, which is set to continue until 8 September 2024 with additional actions and workshops, seeks to draw attention to Kiel's significant role as an arms production hub.

On 1 September 2024, a group of solidarity activists gathered in front of the Carlo Giuliani monument in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin), to protest against what they describe as inhumane prison conditions and for feminist self-determination rights. They also showed solidarity with Gaza.

On 4 September 2024, around a dozen climate activists from Last Generation (Germany) gathered at the airport in Frankfurt am Main (Hessen) for a protest, wearing warning vests, holding signs with messages like 'Oil kills' and 'Stop fossil fuel subsidies,' and demanding greater action from the government on climate protection.

On 5 September 2024, a group of people conducted a protest against the German multinational investment bank, Deutsche Bank AG, in Kiel (Schleswig-Holstein) by displaying banners and a poster with the message 'Siemens, Daimler, Deutsche Bank - the main enemy is at home' on the bank's facade. The protest was organized to criticize the bank's historical and ongoing role in supporting German imperialism and war efforts.

On 5 September 2024, around 30 nurses protested in Munster (Nordrhein-Westfalen) in front of the University Clinic against the establishment of a new nursing chamber. The protesters voiced their opposition to the compulsory membership and monthly fees required for the approximately 230,000 nurses in the state. They argued that the new chamber, intended to improve the quality of care, would not address critical issues such as staff shortages, overwork, and inadequate pay. The protesters called for a referendum on the chamber's establishment, questioning its effectiveness and the burden it places on healthcare workers.

On 31 August 2024, members of the far-right IBD gathered outside a law firm in Dresden (Sachsen), setting up symbolic graves and a poster, objecting to the firm's representation of Issa Al H., the suspected attacker in the Solingen knife attacks, blaming the firm partly for the deaths caused in those attacks.

assoc_actor_1: Anarchist Group (Germany); DKP: German Communist Party; Labor Group (Germany); MLPD: Marxist-Leninist Party of Germany; Ver.di: United Services Union
notes: On 31 August 2024, hundreds of people, including dockworkers, Ver.di, DKP, MLPD, and Anarchists gathered in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg), to protest against the partial sale of the HHLA port logistics company to MSC.
